summary: Herkimer County, NY: wood station tower 1911, Aermotor LL25 steel tower 1916, lookout service ended after 1970; still standing, cab closed to visitors.

facts.design: Aermotor LL25 steel tower (1916); self-supporting staircase added 1936

access.note: Wikipedia says open to the public except the tower cab; no closure notice or current land-manager notice found in the pages read

events.note: Wood fire lookout tower built by the Conservation Commission (Forest Lookouts: station established with a wood tower)
Aermotor LL25 steel tower; 50 ft per Wikipedia, 53 ft per Forest Lookouts
Self-supporting staircase installed to replace the wood ladder added to the outside
Ceased fire lookout operations at the end of the 1970 season as aerial detection increased

evidence.quote: Woodhull Mountain is a 2,359-foot-tall (719 m) mountain in the Adirondack Mountains of New York

evidence.supports: location in the Town of Webb, Herkimer County
evidence.quote: It is located east-southeast of Minnehaha in the Town of Webb in Herkimer County
1911: The station established with a wood tower.

evidence.supports: 1911 wood fire lookout tower built by the Conservation Commission
evidence.quote: In September 1911, a wood fire lookout tower was built on the mountain by the Conservation Commission

evidence.supports: 1916 Aermotor LL25 steel tower built by the Conservation Commission, 50 ft
evidence.quote: In 1916, the Conservation Commission built a 50-foot-tall (15 m) Aermotor LL25 steel tower

evidence.supports: LL-25 was the first standard steel fire tower installed in New York State
evidence.quote: The Aermotor model LL-25 was the first standard steel fire tower installed in New York State.

evidence.supports: lighter than the 1917 design, no stairs, galvanized steel rung ladder up the exterior
evidence.quote: The tower was of a lighter weight than the 1917 design and had no stairs but only a galvanized steel rung ladder up the exterior to get to the top

evidence.supports: staircase described as a tower within a tower
evidence.quote: This staircase was a tower within a tower and was anchored to the original tower
This self-supporting staircase was installed in 1936 to replace the wood ladder that was previously installed

evidence.supports: the wood ladder was added to the outside of the tower
evidence.quote: A wood ladder was later added to the outside of the tower

evidence.supports: 1939 newspaper report mentions the tower at Woodhull Mountain
the 1939 newspaper report is dated December 14, 1939
evidence.quote: December 14, 1939: On complaint of Roy Studor

evidence.supports: a telephone wire cut linked the paper company's office, its camps and the tower
evidence.quote: about 75 feet of telephone wire connecting the McKeever office with the company's camps and the tower at Woodhull Mountain

evidence.supports: ceased fire lookout operations at the end of the 1970 season
evidence.quote: the tower ceased fire lookout operations at the end of the 1970 season

evidence.supports: the tower stopped lookout work as aerial detection increased
evidence.quote: Due to the increased use of aerial detection, the tower ceased fire lookout operations at the end of the 1970 season

evidence.supports: tower still remains; open to the public except the cab
evidence.quote: The tower still remains and is open to the public with the exception of the tower cab

evidence.supports: listed as standing by the Forest Fire Lookout Association

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Forest Lookouts gives the 1916 tower as 53 ft (16.2 m); Wikipedia gives 50 ft (15 m). Not resolved by any third source. The record's 16.2 m is kept, and the story says the sources differ.

sources.title: The Five Various Steel Fire Tower Models Utilized in New York State

notes_for_editor: Record agency (NY DEC, Black River Wild Forest) is not stated in facts: the andyarthur.org page returned HTTP 403 to fetch_text. Current access rests on one Wikipedia sentence; no land-manager page was read. The 1939 newspaper item is a passing mention, not staffing evidence. Height conflict (50 vs 53 ft) left open. NYS digital collection photos of this tower (objects 8192, 8193) returned 403, so no photos were added.
